persons.name: Dr William Bradshaw Egan
persons.note: BORN NEAR LAKE KILLARNEY, COUNTY KERRY, IRELAND, 28 SEPTEMBER 1808 - the best-documented foreign origin in the parcel. Andreas: 'In the fall of 1833 Dr. William Bradshaw Egan came to the city.' He was appointed to the health committee for the South Division on 22 August 1834 and delivered the oration when ground was broken for the Illinois & Michigan Canal on 4 July 1836. He bought the Tremont House block from General Beaubien and built five houses on it, known as Egan's Row - which is why a physician is also one of the town's builders. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 2 times: Tax list of the Town of Chicago, 1833 — “Egan, William Bradshaw” (tax_1833_028, line 80); Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Egan, William Bradshaw” (poll_1834_038, line 207). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals.
